sections.markdown:
## C — Following, merging, crossing and passing space

FACT_ID: sec16-F01 | anchor: A01
Measure following time from when the leading vehicle’s rear passes a fixed roadside point until your vehicle reaches that point. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec16-F02 | anchor: A01
If your vehicle reaches the marker before three seconds pass, fall back and repeat the check until the gap reaches at least three seconds. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec16-F03 | anchor: A01
Some conditions can require more than the baseline following space; the handbook says a four-second gap may be needed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec16-F04 | anchor: A01
Increase following space on slippery roads because stopping takes more distance. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec16-F05 | anchor: A01
If a following driver wants to pass, slow to create room ahead and help the pass finish sooner. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec16-F06 | anchor: A01
Leave extra room behind motorcycles in case the rider falls, particularly on wet, icy, gravel or metal surfaces. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec16-F07 | anchor: A01
Fall farther behind vehicles whose drivers may not see you, including trucks, buses, vans and vehicles towing campers or trailers. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec16-F08 | anchor: A01
A larger gap behind a large vehicle improves the view ahead and the chance of being seen. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec16-F09 | anchor: A01
A heavy load or towed trailer increases stopping distance and calls for more following space. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec16-F10 | anchor: A01
Increase following distance when darkness or bad weather makes the road ahead hard to see. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec16-F11 | anchor: A01
When tailgated, try to create additional space ahead so braking can be less abrupt. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec16-F12 | anchor: A01
Leave extra room behind police, ambulance and fire vehicles because they need operating space. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec16-F13 | anchor: A01
Near rail crossings, leave additional room behind vehicles that must stop there, including transit buses, school buses and hazardous-material carriers. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec16-F14 | anchor: A01
When stopped uphill, leave room for the vehicle ahead to roll backward as it starts. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec16-F15 | anchor: A02
Maintain a steady speed and signal slowing or turns early to help following drivers keep a safe gap. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec16-F16 | anchor: A02
Pick up or release passengers at a safe stopping place outside traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec16-F17 | anchor: A02
Before parallel parking with traffic behind, signal, draw beside the space and allow following vehicles to pass. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec16-F18 | anchor: A02
If necessary slow travel delays others, pull aside safely and let them pass, using a turnout where available. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec16-F19 | anchor: A02
If tailgated and a right lane is available, move right; without one, wait for a clear road ahead and gradually reduce speed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec16-F20 | anchor: A02
Never brake abruptly to discourage a tailgater because this increases rear-impact risk. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec16-F21 | anchor: A02
Maintain side space and avoid remaining alongside another vehicle where it could crowd or enter your lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec16-F22 | anchor: A02
Leave as much safe room as possible from opposing vehicles; on a two-lane road, avoid hugging the center line. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec16-F23 | anchor: A02
The handbook generally recommends driving in the center of the lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec16-F24 | anchor: A02
On a multilane road, make room for entering traffic by moving over when the neighboring lane is clear. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec16-F25 | anchor: A02
Leave extra clearance beside parked cars because doors, pedestrians or the vehicles themselves may enter your path. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec16-F26 | anchor: A02
Allow extra room for pedestrians and cyclists, especially children, because they can enter the path suddenly. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0129]
